606:     /// Heuristic: does this error text look like an unclosed bracket?
607:     fn looks_like_missing_bracket(text: &str) -> bool {
608:         let opens: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == '(' || c == '[' || c == '{').count();
609:         let closes: usize = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == ')' || c == ']' || c == '}').count();
610:         opens > closes
611:     }

613:     /// Detect which bracket types are unbalanced (more opens than closes) in
614:     /// the given error text.
615:     fn bracket_kinds(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
616:         let mut kinds = Vec::new();
617:         for (open, close, kind) in [('(', ')', "("), ('[', ']', "["), ('{', '}', "{")] {
618:             let opens = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == open).count();
619:             let closes = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == close).count();
620:             if opens > closes {
621:                 kinds.push(kind);
622:             }
623:         }
624:         kinds
625:     }

627:     /// Returns the matching opener for a missing closing bracket kind.
628:     fn missing_bracket_opener(kind: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
629:         match kind {
630:             ")" => Some("("),
631:             "]" => Some("["),
632:             "}" => Some("{"),
633:             _ => None,
634:         }
635:     }

637:     /// True if only line terminators, whitespace, `;`, or `,` follow the node
638:     /// before end of file.
639:     fn is_end_of_file(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
640:         source[node.end_byte()..]
641:             .bytes()
642:             .all(|b| matches!(b, b'\n' | b'\r' | b' ' | b'\t' | b';' | b','))

645:     /// True if the node is the last content on its line (only line terminators,
646:     /// whitespace, `;`, or `,` follow it up to the next newline).
647:     fn is_line_ending(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
648:         let rest = &source[node.end_byte()..];
649:         let line_end = rest.find('\n').unwrap_or(rest.len());
650:         rest[..line_end]
651:             .bytes()
652:             .all(|b| matches!(b, b'\r' | b' ' | b'\t' | b';' | b','))
653:     }

655:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
656:     fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
657:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
658:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
659:         let has_opener = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
660:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
661: 
662:         if has_opener && !has_end {
663:             return true;
664:         }
665: 
666:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
667:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
668:             let kind = prev.kind();
669:             if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&kind) {
670:                 return true;
671:             }
672:         }
673: 
674:         false
675:     }

677:     /// True if the given ERROR node appears inside a function call's argument
678:     /// list: either directly inside an `arguments` node whose parent is a
679:     /// `function_call`, or as a sibling of such an `arguments` node within
680:     /// the call.
681:     fn is_in_function_call_args(node: &Node) -> bool {
682:         let mut current = node.parent();
683:         while let Some(ancestor) = current {
684:             match ancestor.kind() {
685:                 "arguments" => {
686:                     return ancestor
687:                         .parent()
688:                         .is_some_and(|p| p.kind() == "function_call");
689:                 }
690:                 "function_call" => {
691:                     // The ERROR is a direct child of the call. It is within the
692:                     // argument list when the call also has an `arguments` child.
693:                     let mut cursor = ancestor.walk();
694:                     return ancestor
695:                         .children(&mut cursor)
696:                         .any(|c| c.kind() == "arguments");
697:                 }
698:                 _ => {}
699:             }
700:             current = ancestor.parent();
701:         }
702:         false
703:     }

705:     /// Classify a missing-END error node into a specific ENDCT variant.
706:     ///
707:     /// Returns the check ID and message for the first matching variant:
708:     /// ENDCT4 (classdef followed by a function definition without a
709:     /// METHODS block), ENDCT2 (a block opener appears in the error text or
710:     /// the previous sibling), or ENDCT3 (the error is followed by a sibling
711:     /// that starts with a block-opening keyword).
712:     fn classify_missing_end(node: &Node, source: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
713:         let start = node.start_byte();
714:         let node_end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
715:         let text = &source[start..node_end];
716:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
717:         let line = node.start_position().row + 1;
718: 
719:         // ENDCT4: ERROR text contains "classdef", a function_definition
720:         // follows it as a sibling, and no "methods" appears between them.
721:         if lower.contains("classdef") {
722:             let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
723:             while let Some(sib) = sibling {
724:                 if sib.kind() == "function_definition" && sib.start_byte() > start {
725:                     let between = &source[node_end..sib.start_byte()];
726:                     if !between.to_lowercase().contains("methods") {
727:                         return Some((
728:                             "ENDCT4",
729:                             "A METHODS block or END might be missing before the function definition. This might be causing additional error messages.".to_string(),
730:                         ));
731:                     }
732:                     break;
733:                 }
734:                 sibling = sib.next_sibling();
735:             }
736:         }
737: 
738:         // ENDCT2: a block opener appears in the ERROR text or its previous
739:         // sibling, and the ERROR does not contain `end`.
740:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
741:         if !has_end {
742:             let opener_in_text = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
743:             let opener_in_prev = node
744:                 .prev_sibling()
745:                 .map(|prev| {
746:                     let prev_text = &source[prev.start_byte()..prev.end_byte()];
747:                     BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| prev_text.to_lowercase().contains(kw))
748:                 })
749:                 .unwrap_or(false);
750:             if opener_in_text || opener_in_prev {
751:                 let raw_end = node.end_position().row;
752:                 let end_line = if source[..node_end].ends_with('\n') {
753:                     raw_end
754:                 } else {
755:                     raw_end + 1
756:                 };
757:                 let opener_line = if opener_in_text {
758:                     line
759:                 } else {
760:                     node.prev_sibling()
761:                         .map(|p| p.start_position().row + 1)
762:                         .unwrap_or(line)
763:                 };
764:                 return Some((
765:                     "ENDCT2",
766:                     format!(
767:                         "An END might be missing (after line {end_line}), possibly matching line {opener_line}."
768:                     ),
769:                 ));
770:             }
771:         }
772: 
773:         // ENDCT3: the ERROR is followed by a sibling that starts with a
774:         // block-opening keyword.
775:         let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
776:         while let Some(sib) = sibling {
777:             let sib_text = &source[sib.start_byte()..sib.end_byte()];
778:             match sib_text.split_whitespace().next() {
779:                 Some(first) if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&first.to_lowercase().as_str()) => {
780:                     let kw = text
781:                         .split_whitespace()
782:                         .next()
783:                         .unwrap_or("")
784:                         .to_uppercase();
785:                     let matched = first.to_uppercase();
786:                     return Some((
787:                         "ENDCT3",
788:                         format!(
789:                             "An END might be missing (before {kw} on line {line}), possibly matching {matched}."
790:                         ),
791:                     ));
792:                 }
793:                 Some(_) => break,
794:                 None => {}
795:             }
796:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
797:         }
798: 
799:         None
800:     }

827:                 } else if !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {

832:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {

834:                     message: format!("Invalid MATLAB file name '{}': {}", name, reason),

837:                     line: 1,

847:     /// Check for class/script structure issues (CLIS, CLTWO, SOFOC, SEMFU).
848:     fn check_file_structure(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
849:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
850:         let mut cursor = root.walk();
851: 
852:         let mut class_count = 0usize;
853:         let mut has_non_class_statements = false;
854:         let mut has_function_def = false;
855:         let mut has_any_real_content = false;
856: 
857:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
858:             let kind = child.kind();
859:             match kind {
860:                 "class_definition" => class_count += 1,
861:                 "function_definition" => {
862:                     has_function_def = true;
863:                     has_any_real_content = true;
864:                 }
865:                 "comment" => {} // Comments don't count as content.
866:                 "expression_statement" => {
867:                     // Check if it's just a semicolon.
868:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
869:                     let trimmed = text.trim();
870:                     if trimmed == ";" {
871:                         // Empty statement — doesn't count as real content.
872:                     } else {
873:                         has_non_class_statements = true;
874:                         has_any_real_content = true;
875:                     }
876:                 }
877:                 _ if !child.is_error() && kind != "\n" => {
878:                     has_non_class_statements = true;
879:                     has_any_real_content = true;
880:                 }
881:                 _ => {}
882:             }
883:         }
884: 
885:         // CLTWO: Multiple class definitions in one file.
886:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLTWO") && class_count > 1 {
887:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
888:                 rule_id: "CLTWO",
889:                 message: format!(
890:                     "File contains {class_count} class definitions; only one is allowed per file"
891:                 ),
892:                 severity: Severity::Error,
893:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
894:                 line: 1,
895:                 column: 1,
896:                 fix: None,
897:             });
898:         }
899: 
900:         // CLIS: Class definition in a script file (non-function statements exist).
901:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLIS")
902:             && class_count > 0
903:             && has_non_class_statements
904:             && !has_function_def
905:         {
906:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
907:                 rule_id: "CLIS",
908:                 message: "Class definition in a script file; statements exist outside the class"
909:                     .to_string(),
910:                 severity: Severity::Error,
911:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
912:                 line: 1,
913:                 column: 1,
914:                 fix: None,
915:             });
916:         }
917: 
918:         // SOFOC: Statements outside a class definition in a class file.
919:         if self.is_check_enabled("SOFOC")
920:             && class_count > 0
921:             && has_non_class_statements
922:             && has_function_def
923:         {
924:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
925:                 rule_id: "SOFOC",
926:                 message:
927:                     "Statements outside class definition in a class file are not allowed"
928:                         .to_string(),
929:                 severity: Severity::Error,
930:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
931:                 line: 1,
932:                 column: 1,
933:                 fix: None,
934:             });
935:         }
936: 
937:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
938:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
939:             && !has_any_real_content
940:             && class_count == 0
941:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
942:         {
943:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
944:             let only_empty = source
945:                 .lines()
946:                 .all(|line| {
947:                     let trimmed = line.trim();
948:                     trimmed.is_empty()
949:                         || trimmed == ";"
950:                         || trimmed.starts_with('%')
951:                 });
952:             if only_empty {
953:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
954:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
955:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
956:                         .to_string(),
957:                     severity: Severity::Error,
958:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
959:                     line: 1,
960:                     column: 1,
961:                     fix: None,
962:                 });
963:             }
964:         }
965: 
966:         diagnostics
967:     }

1069:     /// Recursively walk statements for validation.
1070:     fn walk_statements(
1071:         &self,
1072:         node: Node,
1073:         source: &str,
1074:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
1075:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
1076:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
1077:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
1078:     ) {
1079:         let kind = node.kind();
1080: 
1081:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
1082:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
1083:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
1084:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
1085:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
1086:                     let pos = node.start_position();
1087:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1088:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
1089:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
1090:                         severity: Severity::Error,
1091:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
1092:                         line: pos.row + 1,
1093:                         column: pos.column + 1,
1094:                         fix: None,
1095:                     });
1096:                 }
1097:             }
1098:         }
1099: 
1100:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
1101:         if kind == "function_definition" {
1102:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
1103:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
1104:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
1105:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
1106:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
1107:                 {
1108:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
1109:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1110:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
1111:                         message: format!(
1112:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
1113:                             name
1114:                         ),
1115:                         severity: Severity::Error,
1116:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
1117:                         line: pos.row + 1,
1118:                         column: pos.column + 1,
1119:                         fix: None,
1120:                     });
1121:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
1122:                 }
1123:                 function_names.insert(name);
1124:             }
1125:         }
1126: 
1127:         if kind == "assignment" {
1128:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
1129:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
1130:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
1131:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
1132:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
1133:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
1134:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
1135:                     {
1136:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
1137:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
1138:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
1139:                             message: format!(
1140:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
1141:                                 name

1832:     /// Parse a hex or binary literal into (is_hex, digit count, type suffix).
1833:     fn parse_hex_binary_literal(text: &str) -> Option<(bool, usize, Option<&str>)> {
1834:         let (is_hex, rest) = if text.starts_with("0x") || text.starts_with("0X") {
1835:             (true, &text[2..])
1836:         } else if text.starts_with("0b") || text.starts_with("0B") {
1837:             (false, &text[2..])
1838:         } else {
1839:             return None;
1840:         };
1841: 
1842:         if rest.is_empty() {
1843:             return None;
1844:         }
1845: 
1846:         let suffix = if rest.len() >= 3 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 3..]).is_some()
1847:         {
1848:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 3..])
1849:         } else if rest.len() >= 2 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 2..]).is_some() {
1850:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 2..])
1851:         } else {
1852:             None
1853:         };
1854: 
1855:         let digits = match suffix {
1856:             Some(s) => &rest[..rest.len() - s.len()],
1857:             None => rest,
1858:         };
1859: 
1860:         if digits.is_empty() {
1861:             return None;
1862:         }
1863: 
1864:         Some((is_hex, digits.chars().count(), suffix))
1865:     }

1867:     /// Bit width for a valid type suffix (`u8`/`s8` ... `u64`/`s64`), or None.
1868:     fn suffix_bits(suffix: &str) -> Option<usize> {
1869:         if suffix.len() < 2 {
1870:             return None;
1871:         }
1872:         let kind = suffix.as_bytes()[0];
1873:         let is_valid_kind = kind == b'u' || kind == b'U' || kind == b's' || kind == b'S';
1874:         if !is_valid_kind {
1875:             return None;
1876:         }
1877:         match &suffix[1..] {
1878:             "8" => Some(8),
1879:             "16" => Some(16),
1880:             "32" => Some(32),
1881:             "64" => Some(64),
1882:             _ => None,
1883:         }
1884:     }

1886:     /// Maximum number of digits a type suffix allows for a literal.
1887:     fn max_digits_for_suffix(suffix: &str, is_hex: bool) -> Option<usize> {
1888:         let bits = Self::suffix_bits(suffix)?;
1889:         if is_hex {
1890:             Some(bits / 4)
1891:         } else {
1892:             Some(bits)
1893:         }
1894:     }

1992:     /// Check a call's argument list for name=value syntax with an invalid name

1994:     fn check_name_value(
1995:         &self,
1996:         call: Node,
1997:         args: Option<Node>,
1998:         source: &str,
1999:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
2000:     ) {
2001:         // Assignment shape: `f('Bad Name' = 1)` parses as an assignment whose
2002:         // LHS is a function_call with a MISSING closing paren.
2003:         let is_assignment_lhs = call.parent().is_some_and(|p| {
2004:             p.kind() == "assignment"
2005:                 && p.child_by_field_name("left")
2006:                     .is_some_and(|l| l.id() == call.id())

2009:             call.child(i)
2010:                 .is_some_and(|c| c.is_missing() && c.kind() == ")")
2011:         });
2012:         if is_assignment_lhs && has_missing_paren {
2013:             if let Some(name) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
2014:                 self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
2015:             }
2016:         }
2017: 
2018:         // ERROR shape: an ERROR node containing `=` inside the call's args.
2019:         for e in Self::call_error_nodes(call) {
2020:             let text = &source[e.start_byte()..e.end_byte()];
2021:             if !text.contains('=') {
2022:                 continue;
2023:             }
2024:             let name = if Self::has_string_child(e) {
2025:                 e
2026:             } else if let Some(last) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
2027:                 last
2028:             } else {
2029:                 e
2030:             };
2031:             self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);

2034:         // Direct `=` tokens inside arguments (name=value parses cleanly only

2036:         if let Some(a) = args {
2037:             for i in 0..a.child_count() {
2038:                 if let Some(eq) = a.child(i) {
2039:                     if eq.kind() != "=" {
2040:                         continue;
2041:                     }
2042:                     if let Some(name) = eq.prev_named_sibling() {
2043:                         self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
2044:                     }
2045:                 }
2046:             }
2047:         }
2048:     }
